newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean chipmakers see half-year profits tumble.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean chipmakers see half-year profits tumble.

text.p: Net profits of South Korean chipmakers plunged during the first half of this year, but analysts said on Wednesday their full-year earnings would outpace last year's on an expected rebound in chip prices.
"Their half-year profits were largely in line with earlier estimates and almost in proportion to year-on-year price decreases," said Jeon Woo-jong, an analyst at Dongwon Securities.
LG Semicon Co and Hyundai Electronics Industries Co each posted a drop of about 80 percent in their half-year net profits from a year earlier.

LG Semicon has put its half-year net profit at a provisional 30 billion won ($33.5 million) versus 132.7 billion won a year earlier, and Hyundai Electronics said its net profit fell to 14.8 billion won from 73.1 billion won.
The decline was in proportion to the decline in international prices for 16-megabit DRAMs, the mainstay of computer memory chips, to the $6-$10 range this year from $18-$48 a year earlier.

Companies must officially release their first-half earnings by August 15. Samsung Electronics Co, the world's largest DRAM maker, declined to reveal its earnings figures ahead of this release date, but analysts estimated its half-year net profit at about 100 billion won versus 453.41 billion a year earlier.

"Samsung's profits were helped a lot by earnings from sales of telecommunications equipment for which domestic demand has risen sharply this year," said Oh Jun-young, an analyst at Dongbang Peregrine Securities.
"Otherwise, the company's profits would have been much lower because of the heavy burden of depreciation on its past capital investment," Oh said.
Several new mobile communications services launched this year have sparked a sharp rise in demand for related systems and handsets, analysts said.
This year South Korea launched CT-2 phone services, a hybrid between cordless and celullar phones, and commercial test operations of personal communications services (PCS).
With 16-megabit DRAM prices seen rebounding later this year, full-year earnings of the chipmakers would outpace last year's because prices fell sharply in the second half of last year, analysts said.
The unit price of 16-megabit DRAMs fell to $6 from about $18 in the second half of last year, and analysts said prices should stabilise at about $8 for the rest of this year.
"Recent price cuts by major U.S. computer makers will most likely boost global PC demand later this year," said Oh of Dongbang. "This will keep DRAM prices stable at a relatively high level."
Analysts forecast full-year profits of the chipmakers would increase by about 60 percent. They cited falling production costs as another factor boosting profits.

"Their long chipmaking experience has enabled South Korean makers to sharply lower production costs," said Park Hyi-yeun of Sunkyong Securities. "That means their profit margin would be higher than before even at the same price level."
Last year, Samsung's net profit fell by 93 percent to 164.15 billion won, LG's by 88 percent to 91.1 billion and Hyundai's by 91 percent to 71.14 billion.
